solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A long sentence from Greek letter is made into a book

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A prisoner's long stretch, and something Greek, are turned into a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Life of Pi is Yann Martel's Booker-winning novel, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Made extra circuit in front of electronic light to get a little programme installed

definitions.text: Made extra circuit in front of

indicators.note: software installed goes inside a device, so this word sits within the light

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode
an app is a small application program

explanation.surface: Wiring an extra circuit beside an LED so a small program can be installed.
explanation.walkthrough: The electronics surface makes 'circuit' sound like wiring; it is a lap of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap a rival is to complete a whole extra circuit and pass them from behind.

clue.text: One soldier carrying another in a cargo ship

indicators.note: one who carries something holds it within, so the first soldier goes around the second

parts.note: a fighter is a soldier or combatant
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps, so another soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier carries a wounded comrade aboard a cargo vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship built to carry goods, so a cargo ship.

clue.text: Fruit tree is all dead?

wordplay.note: if all are dead then nought live: O (zero) followed by LIVE

explanation.surface: Someone worrying that their whole fruit tree has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites reading the phrase as 'none live', which splits into the zero shape and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean tree grown for its fruit, so it is a fruit tree.

clue.text: Chickens out of op. Truly agitated

indicators.note: something agitated is shaken up, so these letters are stirred into new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone really nervous, chickening out of an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chickens out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning backs out; split, 'Chickens' is the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry are domestic fowl, of which chickens are the commonest kind.

clue.text: Beat one who acts badly on French sea

parts.note: a ham is a poor, over-the-top actor
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A poor performer gets a beating while out on the French sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer someone is to thrash or batter them, a synonym of beat.

clue.text: Sailor resorted to cannibalism. It finally provides relief

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
cannibals ate men

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of it

explanation.surface: A starving sailor's grim cannibalism at last brings him relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Abatement is a lessening or easing, as in relief from a tax or a pain.

clue.text: Thelonious: first of soul brothers

parts.note: Thelonious Monk was a jazz pianist

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of soul

explanation.surface: Thelonious Monk introduced as the first of the soul brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'soul brothers' look like a music phrase; 'brothers' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks are members of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: They go on … they go on walks!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who talk at length and digress
second meaning: hikers in the countryside

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase looks like a stutter; 'go on' first means talk endlessly, then simply means take part in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is both someone who talks aimlessly and someone who walks for pleasure in the countryside.

clue.text: Valuable record in good cover

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means it sits inside the word for the cover
a cover wraps around whatever it protects, so this word goes outside

parts.note: pious means devout, morally good
REC is the record button on a recorder

explanation.surface: A valuable vinyl record kept safe in a decent sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious is of great worth, the same as valuable.

clue.text: Old lady, capturing wildebeest, shows a lot of bottle!

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so the old lady surrounds the animal

parts.note: mam is a dialect word for mother, one's 'old lady'
the gnu is another name for the wildebeest

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who catches a wildebeest is showing real courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' in British slang means nerve, which is the reading the surface wants; here it is a literal bottle, and a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount, so it contains a lot.

clue.text: March to the French bar … that's sweet!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French word for the month of March
second meaning: a well-known chocolate bar

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like marching up to a French bar; the split comes after 'French'. The Mars bar is a chocolate bar sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for the month of March and also the brand name of a chocolate bar.

clue.text: A comic kind of bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-running British boys' comic, home of Dan Dare
second meaning: a large bird of prey

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a funny species of bird; instead the clue splits after 'comic'. The Eagle was a famous British comic magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the British comic paper and to the large raptor.

clue.text: Weekend warriors surround wild party members at front of level crossing

indicators.note: to surround is to go all round, so the warriors are placed outside the party members

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve soldiers who train at weekends
ravers are people at wild parties

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of level

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers corral partygoers by a level crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level crossing' reads as a railway feature, but the definition is just 'crossing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is a passage across something, which is what a crossing is.

clue.text: Check into an empty Savoy. It's close

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Savoy
a tick is a check mark

explanation.surface: Checking into a deserted Savoy hotel, where the air is stuffy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is a grand London hotel, so 'check into' reads as booking a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and oppressive, which is also called sticky.

clue.text: Hang up near thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to end a phone conversation, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb phrase, the answer means end a telephone conversation; as a set phrase, it is a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a phone conversation is hanging up, and a narrow escape is a near miss, both fitting the phrase.

clue.text: Poet's son writes to the Queen

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to pen is to write
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; 'to' places her after

explanation.surface: A poet's son sends letters to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking definition and wordplay rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, was an Elizabethan poet.

clue.text: No pigs are running around this country

indicators.note: things running around are in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that no pigs roam free in a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is a city-state in Southeast Asia, so it is a country.

clue.text: Breaking up? Great!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: excellent, a British exclamation of delight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone glad about a relationship ending; 'smashing' is also British slang for wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of shattering something and a dated British word for excellent.

clue.text: Kit bag's contents held by Dad's Army's Arthur (formally)

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip

parts.note: Arthur Lowe played Captain Mainwaring in the BBC sitcom Dad's Army; formally he is Mr Lowe

indicators.note: a word's contents are its inner letters, here just the central one

parts.note: the middle letter of bag

explanation.surface: Captain Mainwaring's actor holds the kit bag in Dad's Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the Home Guard. 'Kit bag' reads as one item, but 'Kit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe, the Elizabethan playwright, was known as Kit.

clue.text: European, say, chewed a piece of cake

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: chewed food is mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European, for instance, eating a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something simple to do.

clue.text: Mean to get home with tuppence short of a shilling

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
an old shilling was twelve pence; two pence less is ten pence, written 10d, TEN D

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to get home with nearly a shilling in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had twelve pennies (d) to the shilling, so tuppence short leaves ten d. 'Not a full shilling' also hints at someone a bit simple.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Position is, strangely, last in line

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its normal order, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone finds themselves oddly placed at the back of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last in line' reads as a single position; its words are the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to put it in position, so position is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Genetically modified inside; it's a terrible shame

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other letters
terrible suggests a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
GM is the standard abbreviation for genetically modified

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting the disgrace of genetically modified food.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, a kind of shame.

clue.text: Ducks stand in ponds and start to swim in them

parts.note: a sub is a substitute, someone who stands in

indicators.note: 'in them' places that letter inside the ponds just named

parts.note: meres are small lakes or ponds

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so just that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of swim

explanation.surface: Ducks stand in ponds and then begin swimming about in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is a verb here, not the birds the surface shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to plunge it under water, which is to submerse it.

clue.text: Summit by northern bay

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A hilltop looking over a bay in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a stretch of coast; it is the reddish-brown colour of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay is a reddish-brown colour, especially of horses, so it is a shade of brown.

clue.text: Quiet in the back passage!

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A cheeky request for silence in a rear corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a long narrow passage, as in a mine or lift shaft.

clue.text: One in a suit has flat in the London area

indicators.note: in places the flat within the area

parts.note: SE is a London postcode area, south-east
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit owns a flat in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a suit' suggests a businessman; it is a playing card belonging to one of the four suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Each card of the spades suit in a deck is a spade, so it is one in a suit.

clue.text: I cry and state "We're all under the same pressure here!"

definitions.text: We're all under the same pressure here!

parts.note: taken as written
to sob is to cry
AR is the postal code for Arkansas, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone in tears protesting that everyone is equally stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted remark sounds like workplace stress; read literally, it is a line on a weather map speaking for its points.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather chart joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Follow goal with a G'n'T cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letters of gin and tonic's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Celebrating a goal with a gin and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to follow someone, often uninvited.

clue.text: Softly, with top priority, without hesitation!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is taken away

parts.note: done with top priority is done urgently
ur is a hesitant sound, like er

explanation.surface: An instruction to act quietly, yet urgently and without dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to contradict itself, softly yet top priority; the urgency is just wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gently and softly both describe doing something with a light touch.

clue.text: Succulent, dark bit of breast turned and even cut in half, in the middle

indicators.note: turned round means read from the other end
something put in the middle sits inside the other word

parts.note: the areola is the darker ring around the nipple

indicators.note: cutting a word in half throws away its second half

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook describes a juicy piece of dark breast meat, turned and halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark bit of breast' suggests poultry meat; it is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent plant with thick fleshy leaves storing water.
